name: SoHappyPDF
tagline: Browser-based PDF toolkit: merge, split, compress, convert, sign and edit files without installing desktop software.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: PDF utilities are the most solved problem in software: pdf-lib, pdfjs, Ghostscript and LibreOffice already do everything the paid tools wrap in a progress bar. An agent can wire up merge, split, reorder, rotate, watermark, image-to-PDF, text extraction and page deletion entirely in the browser in one sitting, and files never leave your machine, which is strictly better than uploading a signed contract to someone's S3 bucket. The awkward parts are the ones that need real binaries: aggressive compression wants Ghostscript, and Office-to-PDF wants a headless LibreOffice, so you get a small local sidecar instead of pure web. Scanned-document OCR and true text reflow editing stay genuinely hard. For everything most people actually do with a PDF tool twice a month, the DIY version wins on privacy and loses nothing.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you drop PDFs in and merge, split, reorder, rotate, delete pages, watermark, convert images to PDF and extract text, all client side, with a tiny local server for Ghostscript compression and LibreOffice conversion.
requirements: Ghostscript installed locally for the compress option
LibreOffice installed locally for Office file conversion
Nothing else, no accounts, no cloud
whatYouLose: OCR on scanned documents, which needs Tesseract plus a lot of tuning to be useful
Real text editing and reflow inside an existing PDF, not just annotation overlays
A polished mobile experience and the ability to process a file from someone else's phone
Handling of weird, broken or password-protected PDFs that commercial engines have spent years hardening against
Legally meaningful e-signature workflows with audit trails, if that is part of why you pay
moatNotes: The category moat is being the first result someone remembers when they need a PDF merged at 4pm, not the code.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because nobody wants to install Ghostscript to combine two invoices. Paid PDF sites sell the absence of setup: a URL you already have bookmarked, drag, download, done, from any machine including a work laptop you cannot install anything on. They also absorb the long tail of malformed files, and their conversion engines handle the ugly DOCX with tracked changes that your local LibreOffice will mangle. The privacy trade is real though, and if you handle contracts or medical records, running the same open source libraries yourself is the more defensible choice.
notes: The libraries doing the work here are free and have been for a decade; you are paying for a domain name you can remember.
prompt:
Build a local-first PDF toolkit that runs entirely on my machine. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry, no analytics.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Vite + React + TypeScript for the UI, Tailwind for styling.
- pdf-lib for PDF manipulation, pdfjs-dist for rendering page thumbnails.
- A small Express + TypeScript sidecar on port 8787 for the two jobs that need native binaries.
- pnpm. One repo, two workspaces: web and server.

Client-side features (no server involved, files stay in the browser):
1. Drop zone accepting multiple PDFs and images (png, jpg, webp).
2. Page grid with pdfjs thumbnails: select, reorder by drag, rotate 90/180/270, delete pages.
3. Merge all loaded documents in the current grid order into one PDF.
4. Split: export selected pages as a new PDF, or burst every page into a zip (use jszip).
5. Images to PDF, one image per page, fit to A4 with margins.
6. Text watermark with adjustable opacity, angle, font size, applied to selected pages.
7. Extract plain text per page using pdfjs and offer it as a .txt download.
8. Page numbers stamped bottom-center, configurable start number.
9. Encrypt/decrypt is out of scope, say so in the UI rather than faking it.

Sidecar features (POST multipart, return the file, delete temp files immediately):
- POST /compress: shell out to Ghostscript with screen/ebook/printer quality presets. Return 501 with a clear message if gs is not on PATH.
- POST /convert: shell out to `soffice --headless --convert-to pdf` for docx, xlsx, pptx, odt. Return 501 with a clear message if soffice is missing.
- Reject files over 100MB. No file ever written outside a temp dir.

Requirements:
- Everything works offline after install. No CDN fonts, no external requests at runtime.
- No .env needed, but add one with PORT and MAX_UPLOAD_MB and read it, do not hardcode.
- Vitest tests for the merge, split and rotate helpers using a fixture PDF you generate in the test setup.
- README with install steps, the Ghostscript and LibreOffice prerequisites, and an explicit list of what this does NOT do: OCR, text reflow editing, signatures, repairing corrupt PDFs.
- `pnpm dev` starts both web and sidecar concurrently.
